findings.issue: assertArgs skips global SHELL_META/UNC validation for values consumed by valueFlags. The loop validates the flag token, then jumps i += 2, so the flag value never reaches the universal metachar/path checks.
findings.exploit: On Windows, if codex resolves to a .cmd shim, args like ["exec","-o","C:\\Users\\Vlad\\Desktop\\Claude\\Projects\\WarpOS\\x&calc"] pass because codex -o only checks isInRepo(v). safeSpawnSync then runs cmd.exe /c <codex.cmd> ... and cmd.exe can interpret & as a command separator.
findings.fix: Before accepting a valueFlag value, apply the same universal checks to v unless a tool-specific explicit exception exists. For cmd-shim tools, reject all cmd.exe metacharacters in both flags and values. Also add tests for each valueFlag carrying &, |, $, backtick, CR/LF, spaces, and UNC/absolute executable paths.

findings.issue: codex -o validator permits temp paths and uses startsWith(os.tmpdir()) without a path boundary or metachar rejection.
findings.exploit: A value such as C:\\Users\\Vlad\\AppData\\Local\\TempX\\out passes v.startsWith(os.tmpdir()) even though it is not under the temp dir. A temp path containing cmd metacharacters also passes as a consumed value and can reach cmd.exe for .cmd shims.
findings.fix: Use realpath/path.resolve boundary checks: real === tmp || real.startsWith(tmp + path.sep). Prefer disallowing temp output entirely unless required. Apply SHELL_META to the consumed value.

findings.issue: resolveTool uses PATHEXT entries verbatim. Empty PATHEXT entries or entries without a leading dot can produce unexpected candidates, and PATHEXT is attacker-controlled process environment.
findings.exploit: With a hostile parent env, PATHEXT can alter resolution order or add unusual extensions. The repo/temp/approved-root checks reduce impact, but if approved roots are unset this still broadens executable discovery beyond the intended .COM/.EXE/.BAT/.CMD set.
findings.fix: Ignore process.env.PATHEXT for safety-critical resolution or normalize to a fixed allowlist [.COM,.EXE,.BAT,.CMD] on Windows. Require WARPOS_APPROVED_TOOL_ROOTS in production dispatch.

findings.issue: validateDispatch enforces the build-chain/in-process invariant only through the resolved JSON contract. It does not independently reject build_chain roles dispatched as in-process-agent if the contract is misconfigured or role_overrides re-allow it.
findings.exploit: If dispatch-contract.json class/override accidentally includes in-process-agent in allowed_shapes and omits it from forbidden_shapes, validateDispatch will allow a build_chain role in-process. validateContractFile would catch this only if run as a separate gate; the runtime check itself is not fail-closed against registryAttrs(role).build_chain.
findings.fix: In validateDispatch, after loading registryAttrs(role), unconditionally reject shape === "in-process-agent" when attrs.build_chain is true, regardless of the merged contract. Keep validateContractFile as an integrity check, not the only enforcement.

findings.issue: Key-file bare-value fallback does not flag suspicious bare values before resolveKey returns them with withValue:true.
findings.exploit: A key file containing a bare line like $(calc) is returned as an inert string and resolveKey later marks it suspicious, so it is not executed or leaked by this module. The issue is mainly inconsistent source-level suspicion tracking, not direct execution.
findings.fix: Return source metadata from readSource or parse bare key-file values through the same suspicious path before returning. Ensure callers use probe() or check res.suspicious before injecting withValue into child env.

parsed.summary: FAIL. The exploitable issue is the valueFlag bypass in safe-spawn: consumed flag values skip universal metachar/UNC checks, and codex -o accepts repo/temp paths containing cmd.exe metacharacters. That breaks the stated CVE-2024-27980 residual-risk control for .cmd shims. dotenv parsing is in-code and does not execute values; CLI reporting is label-only. The dispatch contract invariant is validated by validateContractFile, but validateDispatch should enforce build_chain != in-process-agent directly at runtime.
